subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning the skeleton for a ~1.85m humanoid knight: hips, spine chain, neck, head, and a jaw joint under a great helm with a separate chin plate, plus shoulder and elbow joints for the arms.

I'm working out the exact height coordinates for hips, chest, shoulders, neck, head, helm top, and plume, then building the spine as a chain of joints with assigned names and parent relationships. Now I'm setting up the neck, head, and jaw joints positioned relative to the head, and starting on the torso geometry using a loft across the spine chain stations.

For the actual torso and surcoat, I'm defining frustum boxes bound to spine joints for the breastplate, a larger blue surcoat layered over it, plus separate front/back tabard panels extending down from the hips so the legs stay unobstructed, and planning a griffin emblem decal as a textured plane on the front panel.

Still writing SVG code...

Now I'm working on layered pauldrons for the shoulders, positioning the joints symmetrically on both sides.

Naming the forearm joint "elbowL" and tip "wristL", parented to spine3, with role arm. I'll skip separate finger digits to save time and just keep a fist box with a thumb capsule for the gauntlet. For the armor, I'm sweeping tubes along the arm chain with tapering radii, plus a sphere cap at the elbow for the couter and a vambrace detail, all in steel colour.

For the pauldrons, I'm layering three hemisphere-like domes (stacked lames) oriented outward and downward from the shoulder joint, with decreasing radii and slightly offset positions to create a stacked shoulder armor look.

Adding gold torus trim rings...

Simpler approach: I'll cast a ray downward onto the plate's surface to find a hit point, then place the decal there using that result, guarding against a null hit. For the dome shape, I'll use a flattened sphere geometry closed on all sides rather than an open hemisphere, since the open version would show its empty underside.

For the lames I'll stack flattened ellipsoids tilted outward along the arm using a direction vector, scaling each part appropriately. I'm now sketching the gorget as a cylinder at the neck and designing the great helm as a lathe profile -- a flat-topped, slightly tapered cylinder shape positioned at the head, working out the radius and height points along the profile curve.

I'm also adding details like a dark eye slit box on the helm's front, a gold vertical reinforcement band, and a ring of small breath holes on the lower right side of the face.

For the jaw area, I'm placing a small bone-colored chin plate below the helm using a tapered box shape, and considering adding a bevor/gorget piece at the neck using another tapered box frustum.

Working through the skeletal hierarchy, I'm placing a forward-pointing jaw bone joint near the chin, then adding a dark neck capsule mesh between the shoulders and head, with a neck joint parented to the spine and a head joint sitting at the helm's base.

Now for the plume, I'm sketching a tall crimson crest curving from the back of the helm upward and forward using a bezier path, then extruding a thin outline to give it some sideways thickness while keeping it mostly flat and sweeping.

Checking for self-intersection along the tail's inner and outer edges to make sure the mohawk shape stays clean and doesn't overlap itself.

Now I'm setting up the plume with a crimson-to-dark-red gradient and a streaked grain texture, plus a small gold holder at the helm top, then moving on to building the leg joints and limb targets.

Still defining leg armor and knee details...

Adding the hip piece and belt, then checking the surcoat skirt panels front and back don't clip into the legs since they're positioned outward from the leg radius. Now moving to the breastplate for the torso.

I'm planning the cuirass with a gold ridge detail, pelvis/torso/chest mapped to the spine joints, and thinking through how to paint the steel with mottled scratches and dents for a weathered look.

Finishing the scratch condition, then I'm sticking to just the few core exported helpers like noise, paint, mottle, gradient, grain, countershade, and stripes rather than risking unsupported imports. For the cape, I'm planning to build it as an extruded torn outline on a back plane rather than a full membrane, positioning it behind the shoulders.

Writing membrane geometry...

Adding gold shoulder clasps as small discs, then plotting the cape's upper edge across the back with a curved path of points. Now I'm positioning the shield on his left arm, working out the wrist coordinates to anchor it.

For the shield's extrusion, I'm choosing a thickness axis along z while laying out the kite-shaped outline in the x-y plane, defining its tall, tapered silhouette point by point with a pointed base.

I'm positioning the shield in front of the left forearm, checking its vertical span against the arm position and nudging its depth placement so it clears the pauldron radius without clipping into the torso.

Checking for overlap between the shield and pauldron near the upper-left corner, I decide to nudge the shield's x position slightly to 0.52 to reduce the collision. For the shield's rim, I'm planning to add a gold border by extruding a second, slightly larger outline behind the main shield shape.

Working out the layering now — gold rim scaled up around 1.05-1.07x sits slightly behind, with the blue shield face offset forward so it stands proud by about 0.025 units, and the griffin emblem plane placed in front of everything at roughly z=0.144 with a size around 0.34.

For the shield, I'm adding scratch detailing in lighter silver/blue over the base paint, and connecting it to the shoulder via an elbow joint bone for posing.

Now considering the sword in the right hand: deciding between a point-up resting grip near the wrist versus a point-down pose, weighing how tall the blade would read against the plume and whether it reaches the ground.

Settling on an angled forward-up pose for a heroic look, with the blade tip extending outward and up from the hand. I'm building the sword from a cylindrical grip, a pommel sphere, a box crossguard, and a tapered blade shape narrowing toward the tip.

Still shaping the blade geometry...

I'm positioning the sword relative to the hand: setting the grip at the right wrist location and defining a normalized direction vector so I can compute points along the blade using hand + direction*t, placing the guard near the base.

For the fist, I'm using a small box around the hand to represent the gauntlet, attached to the wrist bone tip joint. I check that the blade direction doesn't awkwardly intersect the body, and set up the left hand similarly as a gripping fist near the shield strap, positioned slightly behind the shield's front face.

I'm skipping boots and spurs for now, just checking that the foot sole sits flush with the ground plane. For decoration, I'm adding a gold swirl filigree pattern as an SVG texture on the pauldrons, and considering a lathe-generated steel gorget ring around the neck with a cup-like profile shape.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: assigning roles to each joint (hips as spine root, neck, head, jaw) and setting up chains for the spine, arms, and legs with proper parenting. The arm chains need shoulder-elbow-wrist joints named by side (L/R), and since the three arm points aren't collinear, I'm deciding whether to use a simple polyline or a smooth curve through them.

Placing the neck joint at the top of the spine chain, with the head above it and the helmet positioned slightly below the head joint, and setting the eye height relative to the helmet position.

For the torso, I'm shaping the chest breastplate as a tapered box attached to the spine, broader at the top than the waist. I'm considering adding a front ridge or keel for pectoral definition, but realizing it'll mostly be hidden under the surcoat panel anyway, so I can skip that detail.

Instead, I'm making the tabard/surcoat the primary torso covering in blue, slightly narrower than the steel torso frame so steel edges peek out at the sides. Then I'm adding a leather belt across the front with a gold buckle, positioned in front of the tabard surface.

I'm placing the emblem texture plane just slightly in front of the tabard face, and deciding to skip a mirrored back panel since the cape drapes down low enough to cover that area entirely. Now I'm planning the faulds that hang below the belt.

For the tabard itself, I'm splitting it into two bound pieces riding on different bones so it flexes naturally with the hips: an upper section tied to the spine and a wider lower skirt tied to the hips, reaching knee height. I'm adding a gold hem trim at the bottom edge, and painting the surcoat in a mottled deep blue tone for texture variation.

Now I'm sketching out the griffin SVG: a silver body with darker outline, building up the shape from an ellipse-based torso, a round head, a gold beak, and planning out wings, tail, and legs to compose a stylized heraldic creature within the viewBox.

Still writing SVG paths...

I need to position the decal at the top lame center of the plate, and figure out the correct `up` vector so the drawing orientation doesn't go degenerate against the normal direction—settling on [0,0,1] for a sensible top-facing orientation. For the cape, I'm deciding against adding extra torn patch pieces beyond the zigzag edge, and working out the z-depth placement for the back torso section.

Now I'm defining the catmull-rom control points for the cape's upper edge near the shoulders, then computing a jagged, torn-looking lower edge (edge B) using alternating heights and some sine-based variation to create irregular tongue-like tears along the hem.

I'm checking that the cape's resampling by arc length handles the zigzag geometry smoothly, confirming the cape's bone rigging, thickness, and double-sided mesh setup are reasonable, and verifying the drape curvature between the two edges looks right and stays clear of the floor. Now I'm working out the pauldron placement per shoulder side, stacking layered discs with slightly offset centers and radii.

Still refining stacking parameters...

The ring sits at the ellipsoid's equator, sharing the same tilt direction so orientation stays consistent between parts, with flat shading for the low-poly aesthetic. Now I'm working out the pauldron placement, positioning its top near y=1.62 based on the shoulder radius.

Checking the gorget radius against the pauldron's inner edge, then planning the elbow cop as a gold-trimmed steel sphere at the elbow joint, and considering banded coloring for the vambrace -- dark mail for the upper arm under the pauldron, steel for the forearm.

I'll use a tapering radius function across the full arm length, with round caps so the elbow sphere hides the seam between the two sweep segments. For legs I'll apply similar logic, starting with the thigh in MAIL color.

Now sketching the leg geometry: steel-painted sweep with tapered radius, a gold-rimmed poleyn at the knee, possible ankle greave band, and a flat-box sabaton for the foot. For hands I'll build dark steel gauntlet boxes positioned at each wrist tip, and add a gold brow band torus wrapped around the base of the helm.

Still computing helm surface geometry...

Still placing geometry details...

Still shaping the plume outline...

Now I'm thinking through the shield design, adding an emblem and gold rim, and working out the exact z-depth layering so the blue face, rim, and boss sit at the right positions relative to the shield plane.

Writing the kite outline helper function...

Now thinking through the shield and sword placement: shield on the left forearm, sword on the right side.

I'm defining a strap bone rod connecting forearm to shield back, then considering rig details like chain roles and leg contact points. For the steel material, I'm writing a paint function that layers scratches, dents, and rust using coordinate-based noise checks before falling back to the base color.

Now I'm settling on a palette: various steel grays for base, dent, and scratch highlights, a warm rust tone, dark leather brown, mail gray, and accent colors like gold and crimson for trim.

Setting up the knight builder with its imports and starting the construction code...

Building the skeleton joints and chain hierarchy for hips, spine, neck, and head...

I check the overlap math and confirm the bevor sticks out slightly in front as a lower jaw guard with a gold edge, which works fine. Then I sketch the helm using a lathed profile around the head bone, confirming the loop closes properly back to the starting point.

Now I'm building the arm chains for both sides, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints with a fallback value in case the elbow's sweep parameter is undefined, then moving on to set up the hip and leg points using similar limb logic.

Writing leg chain code...

Still writing cape and tabard geometry...

I should split the gold trim rod across both bones, one spanning the upper torso and one at the hips, rather than a single rigid rod. For the blue coloring, I'll use a mottled paint function blending two dark blues for a worn, torn fabric look, and then I'm planning to place the griffin emblem as a textured plane mounted on the mid bone at chest height.

Now I'm designing the sword: the grip as a leather-wrapped rod on the hand bone, a gold pommel sphere, a box-shaped guard oriented along the direction vector, and a tapering frustum blade extending outward.

Checking the sword tip position against the right hand's offset, then sketching simple box geometry for the gauntlet fists at the wrists. Confirming the floor and skirt clearances look fine before finalizing the code.

Still adding helm rings and decal placement...
